reason: Reproduced on both grounds at both sizes and it survives every refutation I could mount. Driven at ?v=paper and ?v=ink, 1440x960 and 390x844: click #b-empty-date, type "3 October 2026" keystroke by keystroke, press Enter. The harvest is byte-identical before and after in all four runs - value "3 October 2026", aria-invalid null, hint still "For example, 3 October 2026.", heading still "When is the day?", no count, no live-region text change, focus still b-empty-date, zero page errors. The same string via the button replaces the screen: 79 / "Saturday 3 October 2026" / "TODAY IS 16 JULY", hint becomes "The day is set. Moments come next.", focus moves to Add a moment. So the button path is whole and Enter is inert, identically on paper and ink. NOT already handled: the input is bare (inp.form false, closest("form") false, no enterkeyhint, no inputmode, no on: block at render-b.js:1585-1589); the only listener is the delegated click at 1596. NOT a restated gate: interaction-check.mjs presses Enter on #b-edit-date (lines 1049/1066/1078) and on an untouched field (2393) but never on #b-empty-date - it only ever fill()s it and clicks the button. NOT in SETTLED (the three owner-empty items there are the draft publish path, the answered-frame stack and the untitled row). And the inconsistency is worse than the finding states: I drove #b-edit-title too - typing and pressing Enter there commits through the native change event ("Renamed to Send the invitations X." in history, row retitled). So Enter commits in two of the product's three text inputs and is dead only in the first one a new owner ever meets, on a single-question screen whose entire job is to take one answer. Against the audience named in the brief - someone who has never used a tool like this - and north star 3, a lone field where the universal answering reflex yields no motion, no refusal and no explanation is a defect at 9.5; Linear, Stripe and Vercel all submit a single-field form on Enter. On the risk the brief asked me to weigh: there is none. The fix routes through the identical handler, so nothing is bypassed - I drove the button with partial input and the refusal path holds ("3" -> aria-invalid true, "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026."; "1 January 2026" -> "That day has gone. Pick one still ahead."; empty -> "Type the day first."), each keeping focus in the field. Half-typed strings that already parse ("3 Oct", "3 October") commit to the same 79 days through the button today, so Enter adds no new leniency whatsoever. One real hazard I did find and the fix must guard: after the day is set focus lands on the Add a moment button, and Enter there opens the editor (verified: editorOpen true, 2 items, focus b-edit-title). An auto-repeating held Enter would therefore chain two screens.
sharpenedFix: Take the finding's keydown listener on #b-empty-date, with three additions. (1) Guard the repeat cascade: `if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.repeat || event.isComposing) return;` - without event.repeat a held Enter commits the day and then activates the newly focused "Add a moment", jumping the owner two screens into an open editor (measured). (2) Keep the delegation intact - event.preventDefault() then node.querySelector('[data-act="setday"]').click(), so all three refusal sentences, the aria-invalid write, the screen replacement and the focus move are inherited byte for byte and no second code path exists. (3) Add enterkeyhint="go" to the input spec: on the phone the field has no form and no hint attribute, so the return key is unlabelled; the listener alone makes Enter work but still leaves the key on a 390-wide keyboard unadvertised. Then add the assertion the gate is missing - focus #b-empty-date, type a valid date, press Enter, assert the count screen renders and focus is on Add a moment; press Enter on "3" and assert aria-invalid="true" with "That is not a date." - on both variants.
